title: Reese The Beast is Simply Too Tough for the NY Bench
meta_description: With 1:30 left, Canada's step-back three made it 87-77. The Dream beat the Liberty 92-82 to lead 1-0.
hook: With 1:30 left and New York still hanging around, Angel Reese kicked it out to Jordin Canada, who stepped back and buried a three to make it 87-77. That was the dagger in a 92-82 Atlanta Dream win in Game 1 of the semis. And get this: the New York Liberty went a perfect 15-of-15 at the line and still lost by 10, because they scored zero fast-break points and coughed it up 21 times. Want to know who kept taking the ball? Reese got steals off four different Liberty players.
summary: Atlanta Dream 92, New York Liberty 82, on October 4, 2026, at State Farm Arena. Atlanta leads the best-of-five 1-0. Body is Ryan's bot draft, edited against ESPN game 401918295. One play was wrong: Reese's layup at 3:43 drew a foul, and she missed the free throw, so it was not a made and-one. Subhead 'Reese the best' is now 'Reese's night'.

unique: Canada's step-back three at 1:30 made it 87-77, after Reese's layup at 3:43 and a missed free throw
New York went 15-of-15 at the line, scored 0 fast-break points, and committed 21 turnovers in a 92-82 loss
Reese's four steals came against Johannes, Stewart, Han Xu, and Fiebich, with the clocks from the play-by-play
Atlanta's 20-2 third-quarter run ended 59-45 on back-to-back Canada layups at 4:05
unverified: The Game 2 prediction and the line that Reese is tougher than anybody on the New York bench are opinion.
The lead photo is from May 22, 2026, at Gateway Center Arena, not from this game. The caption says so.

categories.name: Accuracy

The draft's made and-one at 3:43 was wrong and is now a layup plus a missed free throw.

categories.name: Information gain
categories.reason: The page keeps the possession-by-possession close, including who Reese stole from and when, the missed free throw, and the 20-2 run ending 59-45. Wire recaps have the final and Canada's 25 points. They do not walk the four steals.

categories.name: Effort and replication cost
categories.reason: Every number was checked against the ESPN feed and one injury story. There is no original chart, courtside note, or photo from this game, so another editor with the same feed could rebuild it.

categories.name: Originality
categories.reason: The angle is Reese taking the ball and Canada burying the three, plus a straight Game 2 take. It is not a wire rewrite, and it is still a game recap.

categories.name: Experience and expertise
categories.reason: Ryan Moalemi's byline links to his real author page, and he edits the site. He was not at State Farm Arena, so this is not a courtside report.

categories.name: Main content and layout
categories.reason: The title and H1 match and do not oversell the score. The hook gives the 87-77 three, the 92-82 final, and the perfect free-throw line before the photo. No placeholders.

categories.name: Transparency

categories.name: Writing craft
categories.reason: Short sentences, no em dashes, and real subheads. In-article links open in a new tab. 'Reese the best' was renamed 'Reese's night'.

categories.name: People-first purpose

categories.name: Human voice
categories.reason: No stock AI phrases. The voice is specific and opinionated ('And get this', 'Simple as that', 'My take'). The last paragraph is a group of three, and it was kept because it is the draft's series take.
